newsitem.title: FRANCE: AlliedSignal seeks to expand after market business.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal seeks to expand after market business.

text.p: AlliedSignal Automotive, the car unit of AlliedSignal Inc, plans to expand "after market" business to half of its activities over the next three years, automotive unit chief John Barter said on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters at the Paris car show, Barter said the company will use acquisitions and new products to become less dependent on its "original equipment" business which now accounts for about 60 percent of overall business.

AlliedSignal, the world"s largest maker of turbocharging systems for gas and diesel driven engines, plans to expand its turbocharging business with a six million dollar investment in its plant in Lorraine, lifting capacity to 6,000 turbos a day from 5,000 by March 1997.
Barter said his company is also working to develop "smart" restraint systems which will adjust according to the size of a car passenger and the magnitude of a crash.
He said he plans to first market the system in 1999.
Lawrence Bossiday, Allied Signal chairman said the company"s automotive business will report sales of about four billion dollars this year.
